title: 1975-11-05_SECTION_013_15.txt
concise_summary: PKD argues that his March 1974 experiences constituted a personal preview of the Parousia — the Second Coming of Christ — rather than the Parousia itself in linear time, resolving his earlier confusion by deploying Heraclitus's distinction between the idios kosmos (private world) and the koinos kosmos (shared world). He identifies his 2-3-74 visions as entry into sacred, eternal time that allowed him to witness eschatological realities not yet manifest for all humanity, and interprets TEARS (Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said, 1970) as prophetic fiction that prefigured the historic events of 1974. The entry also pivots to political paranoia, framing his 1974 defiance of the "Xerox letter" and his resistance to Stanislaw Lem and Franz Rottensteiner as divinely orchestrated maneuvers to preserve his independence as a writer, masterminded from a supralunar realm.
key_claims: PKD's 2-3-74 experience was not the Parousia itself in linear time but a personal preview of it — he was 'lifted up into sacred eternal time' as an adult lifts a child to witness a parade, allowing him to see what the full Parousia will show everyone.

Heraclitus's distinction between idios kosmos (private world) and koinos kosmos (shared world) is the only framework that can explain how PKD alone could have had a genuine eschatological experience while others did not.

The Parousia refers specifically to a Second Incarnation — 'St. Sophia being born again' — not merely the spiritual presence of the Cosmic Christ, and this incarnation is still future for the world at large.

PKD was judged acceptable by God not on his own merits but because Christ stood in his place and bore the judgment for him — a formulation explicitly aligned with Martin Luther's theology of imputed righteousness.

His novel TEARS, written in 1970, prophetically paralleled the historic events of 1974 including the slave state, divine intervention, and the removal of the satanic 'kingpin of evil' (implicitly Nixon).

The phosphene activity and drop in GABA he experienced in 3-74 triggered anamnesis — a restoration of memory of his true identity, mission, and cosmic destiny — and reconnected him to the 'plasmatic atmospheric entities.'
recurring_concepts: Idios kosmos / koinos kosmos (Heraclitean distinction between private and shared world)
Sacred eternal time vs. linear time
The Iron City / City of Man vs. the Palm Tree Kingdom / City of God (Augustinian two-cities framework)
Imputed righteousness (Lutheran theology: God sees Christ's perfection in place of the sinner)
The Cosmic Christ as resurrected spirit distinct from incarnate Jesus
people_entities: Augustine of Hippo — patristic theologian cited for his doctrine that at the Parousia the City of Man and City of God will become visibly separate
Martin Luther — cited via the Encyclopaedia Britannica for the doctrine that when God judges the sinner He sees His own perfect Son
Teilhard de Chardin — cited and implicitly corrected: PKD distinguishes the Cosmic Christ's spiritual presence (which Teilhard addresses) from the literal Second Incarnation PKD expects
Heraclitus — pre-Socratic philosopher whose idios/koinos kosmos distinction PKD uses to resolve his central confusion about the privacy of his eschatological experience
Stanislaw Lem — Polish science fiction author and critic described as part of a Marxist critical conspiracy to subject PKD's work to 'structured critics' and destroy his independence
Franz Rottensteiner — Lem's literary agent, named by 'Jack Vann' as one of the desired Marxist critics who would have 'doomed' PKD
Jack Vann (Jack Vance?) — named as a source who identified Lem and Rottensteiner as the intended critics; likely Jack Vance, PKD's friend
Joe Hill — labor movement martyr; PKD was singing Joe Hill's final statement in a dream about being released from prison
Peter — a man with a shaved head at X-Kalay (a drug rehabilitation commune in Canada) to whom PKD gave his radio as an act of instinctive exchange/barter
Senator Lowell Weicker — U.S. Senator whose speech about loving enemies PKD identifies as the 'initial turn of direction' following the divine intervention of 1974
Nixon, Richard — implicitly identified as the 'kingpin of evil,' the satanic figure whose removal was necessary for the divine intervention
Daniel (biblical) — cited alongside John as a prophetic apocalyptist whose mode of visionary perception parallels PKD's own
John (biblical) — the author of Revelation, cited as a precedent for PKD's own apocalyptic witnessing
texts_works: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said (PKD, 1970/1974) — referred to as TEARS; argued to prophetically parallel the events of 1974
Ubik (PKD, 1969) — referenced in the context of Lem's article about PKD's work and Marxist critical intentions
Encyclopaedia Britannica — cited for its account of Luther's doctrine of imputed righteousness
Matthew (Gospel) — cited for the herald angels who foretell the Second Advent
The Book of Daniel (Hebrew Bible/Old Testament) — cited as a model for PKD's apocalyptic vision
The Book of Revelation (New Testament) — implied through reference to John as apocalyptist
autobiographical: In August 1974, PKD experienced the 'pale white light' which he interprets as the moment of divine judgment finding him acceptable.
In March 1974 (2-3-74), PKD underwent what he calls end-time changes — an elaborate reshaping of his character and faculties that he believes prepared him for divine encounter.

PKD dreamed of being released from prison on March 21st, tasked with writing his 300,000-word theological exegesis, and interprets this as confirmation that the U.S. government had a vested interest in suppressing his writing.

PKD had a vision or dream of himself as a crab — a creature that instinctively tries to give something back whenever it receives, never accumulating profit — which he takes as a divine revelation of his essential character.
PKD describes giving his radio to a man named Peter (with a shaved head) at X-Kalay, an act he recalls as emblematic of his lifelong failure to accrue or profit.

PKD received the 'Xerox letter' (a letter apparently from U.S. authorities) which he defied, interpreting this defiance as the first step in a divinely masterminded sequence of evasions to preserve his independence.
PKD reports a 'James, James' dream in which advance scouts of the Afrika Corps rolled into manifestation, which he reads as a vision of the imminent Second Advent.
In February 1975 (2-75), PKD saw the 'palm tree kingdom' which he identifies as the City of God, contrasting with the Iron City of Rome/the slave state.
PKD recounts that his period of independence would have ended in spring 1974 in 'a purely deterministic, karma-dominated world' but for divine intervention.
theological_motifs: Parousia — the Second Coming/Second Advent of Christ as a future literal incarnation
Second Incarnation as 'St. Sophia being born again' — a feminized/Sophianic Christology
Imputed righteousness (Lutheran) — God's judgment sees Christ in place of the sinner
Anamnesis — Platonic/Gnostic restoration of suppressed memory of divine origin and mission
The Two Cities (Augustinian) — City of Man (Iron City/Rome/prison) versus City of God (palm tree kingdom/garden)
Sacred/eternal time vs. linear time — the eschatological present accessible only through enhanced perception
The Elect — a hidden community of persons who underwent the same internal end-time changes as PKD but remain invisible and mute
The Paraclete — the Holy Spirit as rescuer/redeemer whose arrival PKD had long anticipated
Herald angels (Matthean) — presently active forerunners of the coming incarnation
The mustard seed parable — Christ's first incarnation as a tiny seed whose harvest Christ-as-Judge will reap at the end
Apocalypticism — PKD self-identifies as an apocalyptist in the tradition of John and Daniel, seeing with 'aided eyes' what others cannot yet see
literary_self_ref: PKD argues that TEARS (Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said, written 1970) 'parallels exactly the events of 1974': the slave state, the reduction to total despair, divine intervention, judgment, and the implied removal of one evil man followed by the withering away of the state.
PKD links the scene in TEARS at the 'all-night gas station with the black man' to the real-world moment of divine love manifesting through Senator Weicker's speech about enemies being loved.
Ubik is cited in the context of Lem's introductory essay, which PKD interprets as evidence of a Marxist critical conspiracy to subordinate his work to ideological critique.

PKD frames his entire body of fiction as potentially at risk — had the Marxist critics succeeded, 'he would never have been his own man again' — implying his fictional output is inseparable from his divine mission and independent identity.
symbols_images: The pale white light — the signal of divine judgment that PKD experienced in August 1974
The crab — PKD's vision of himself as a creature that instinctively gives back whatever it receives, never accumulating, representing his core character of honest exchange over profit
The Iron City / Rome — the City of Man, the slave state, the prison: the visible face of worldly power and evil
The palm tree kingdom — the City of God, the garden: the eschatological realm PKD glimpsed in February 1975
The veil — Augustinian image: at the Parousia the veil lifts and the two cities become visibly distinct
The parade — PKD's metaphor for his privileged eschatological viewpoint: an adult lifting a child to see over the crowd, a temporary elevation into sacred time
The mustard seed — Christ's first incarnation as a small seed; the final judgment as the harvest
The Afrika Corps scouts — appearing in the 'James, James' dream as figures heralding the imminent Second Advent
The defective lamb — a damaged creature whose 'smashing-down' signals the arrival of the Second Advent
Prison / release from prison — recurring image in PKD's dream of March 21st, his captivity under political/institutional power and his liberation to write
The shaved head of Peter at X-Kalay — a specific memory-image of PKD's instinctive generosity and non-accumulation
tensions: PKD initially asserts that the Parousia has arrived, then immediately revises: 'No, I guess the Parousia hasn't come yet in linear time' — the Heraclitean idios/koinos distinction is introduced to resolve but also marks this as a genuine self-correction mid-entry.

PKD claims his 3-74 experience was 'real' and constituted genuine encounter with the eschatological, while simultaneously acknowledging that others could not share or verify it — the private nature of the experience sits in tension with its claimed cosmic significance.

PKD frames himself as both passive recipient (God shaped him, stood in his place, masterminded his actions) and as an agent making consequential defiant choices (the Xerox letter, resistance to Lem). The two stances are not fully reconciled.

The claim that 'herald angels are here already' and the Parousia is imminent sits alongside the acknowledgment that the Second Incarnation is 'still future' — the imminence varies within the same entry.

PKD says he was made acceptable by God not due to his own merits, then immediately describes the virtuous character revealed by the crab-vision as a form of personal virtue ('An honest creature') — the Lutheran erasure of merit and the affirmation of intrinsic character coexist uneasily.

The political-paranoia section (Lem, Rottensteiner, the U.S. government suppressing his writing) is asserted with the same confidence as the theological revelations, but the evidential basis is conspicuously thinner — a scholarly reader must flag this as a category-shift within the entry.
evidence_quotes: I was lifted up (into sacred eternal time) the way an adult lifts a child to witnes a parade; I saw it the way John and Daniel saw it; I am an apocalyptist.
Without the distinction of Heraclitus it is impossible to comprehend or explain how I could have the experience, and it be real, and others could not.
When God judged me God saw His own perfect & spotless son, and so found me acceptable. But by then there was enough of me to make the judgment just.

The phosphere activity, drop in GABA, signalled anamnesis: memory restored of who I was (secondarily, why I was here). Thus I could not, would not, do what the Xerox letter et al. demanded. My true self & destiny were recalled (to me).
In a purely deterministic, karma-dominated world, my period of independence would have ended in the spring of 74.
uncertainty_flags: 'Jack Vann' is almost certainly Jack Vance (PKD's friend and fellow SF author), but the name as written is ambiguous and could refer to another figure — the identification should be verified against the broader Exegesis and correspondence.

The 'Xerox letter' is referenced as a known entity but never explained in this segment — it presumably refers to a letter from U.S. law enforcement or intelligence that PKD interpreted as a threat, but the document itself remains unverified; its content and sender are unclear from this passage alone.

The 'James, James' dream in which Afrika Corps scouts appear is invoked as prophetic evidence, but the connection between Rommel's army and the Second Advent is asserted without elaboration — the interpretive logic is opaque.

PKD's claim that the Parousia refers to a literal 'St. Sophia being born again' (a second physical incarnation as a feminine divine figure) contradicts most Christian theological traditions and Teilhard de Chardin's Omega Point framework, which PKD dismisses but does not fully engage.

The passage is truncated mid-sentence ('In analyzing the situation then I would') — the argument about karma and determinism is interrupted, and the reader cannot determine the conclusion PKD was building toward.

PKD identifies Nixon only implicitly as 'Satan at the heart of the citadel' and 'one evil man' — the identification is strongly implied by context (the 1974 Watergate/resignation events) but never stated by name in this segment.

So I say that TEARS, which was written in 1970, parallels exactly the events of 1974: in depicting the slave state, the reduc¬y tion to total despair followed by abrupt intervention and judgment, the (implied) removal of one man and finally the withering away of the state after the manifestation of love. It is as if the reign of power is followed by the reign of love, the latter entering the world from Heaven, and requiring for its manifestation the removal of one evil man — which is to say Satan at the heart of the citadel. -1- But subjectively speaking, the most astonishing events, in contrast to the great historic intervention plus the material in TEARS, were the elaborate changes made in me, end-time changes I am certain, the shaping me up to make me acceptable — for the day which in August did come (the pale white light). If there had been no historic changes or perceptions of them; if there had been no TEARS, what was left was still overwhelmingly miraculous and complicated and unprecedented...that is probably the most remarkable aspect of it: unprecedented. The only way my theory about the Parousia having arrived could be wrong would be if somehow I experienced it in ad¬y vance, a sort of mini-Parousia, but this does not accord with the fact of the great historic intervention, which was anything but mini and personal and subjective. I was brought up to —I can't say attained— certain extraordinary levels of character, as well as given certain extraordinary perceptions and insights — which fits, as an event, a sub-event, with the matrix event: the Second Coming, around which everything else revolves as planets around a sun. My involvement in this great event is certainly there, although uncertain (to me). What role did I play? Who was I? Especially the latter. Who was I historically or supernaturally? I certainly was not myself at that time; I was taken over. Those were momentous days, and therein lies the fact: uniquely momentous days in the history of the world & in my experience as well. It must be that others, many other persons, were brought around, changed, to reach their absolute best, for this occasion, but I can know that only as an article of faith; they are as mute as I. Who can I tell? Who can they tell? There must be a Christian community, a body of the faithful (the elect?) who experienced the crucial changes I experienced...but it is all internal, the changes, the judgment (or awareness of it, anyhow), and the results of that judgment, which are for the future. Perhaps we are supposed to be —remain— invisible. I have the greatest knowledge of all: that when he judged me, the Lord found me acceptable, but I also know that I was acceptable because —my godl— He stood in my place and was acceptor of the judgment in my stead I It all fits; it was He, and He judged; and as the EB says about Luther's view, when God judged me God saw His own perfect & spotless son, and so found me acceptable. But by then there was enough of me to make the judgment just. I had come to be what he had shaped me to be. And he did not do it because I was good; if I had been good he wouldn't have had to do it, change me... so no use seeking to identify my special merits. It was due to his love, his mercy. And, most of all, rescue: for someone who believed with all his heart —had faith— that someday the Paraclete would come to his door with that very rescue & redemption. But in the vision of me as the crab I saw myself as He sees me: the crab who when given or offered something turns to what it has to give something back, not to profit but to exchange in barter: an honest creature, not bright enough to take without trying to give back, perhaps; never acquiring because with each new accrition it has given back something equal, thus keeping only a constant ratio, never gain. Never besting; never getting the better of. And thus I see my whole life as it is. A virtue. I never got the hang of accrual, of profit. When the Parousia comes it can be seen with the unaided eye; whereas I needed aided eyes, enhanced percep¬y tion, to see what I witnessed. So, again: I did not reach or attain this condition; it reached down (back) to me. In attempting to determine the relationship between the events I saw and the world of linear time in which we live, I have the verbal statemtn, "St. Sophia will be born again etc." to go on, indicating that these events lie directly ahead, since the rebirth of St. Sophia is in itself the Parousia or Second Advent. The Parousia refers not to the presence of the Cosmic Christ, but to the Second Incarnation, reffered to as "St. Sophia being born again," Teilhard de Chardin to the contrary. Thus he/she/it will be visible to all, with unaided eyes. The Cosmic Christ, as resurrected spirit, is indeed present now (it was he probably who came to me, as Holy Spirit), but to our normal eyes nothing is visible; he can only enter inside, as does the Holy Spirit, not be visible as he was as Jesus, and will be again (incarnated in a physical body); but preparations are now being made: the anticipation & expectation are high; the herald angels are here already. Mankind, all of them, will see with unaided eyes precisely what I saw with aided (enhanced) eyes, such as the transformation of the animals; the dividing apartly clearly of the City of Man versus the City of God; the pale white light coming on which signals judgment, etc. This finally resolves my confusion as to what I saw, which was manifestly now, and the promise of a future rebirth. However powerful, actual and real the spirit is (the Cosmic Christ is), this constitutes no incarnation, and it specifically, with a fine economy of words, is an incarnation that was promised (foretold). The foretelling is by herald angels (v. Mathew). The event itself is still future (for all to experience). This was, of course, a Christian rebirth for me (3-74), a being born again from above; but the material I witnessed had specific content beyond the personal experience itself. I recall the "James, James" dream in which advance scouts of the Afrika Corps rolled into manifestation; this was the Second Advent, which I requested medical help from. The implication of this dream was that it would come soon. It came upon the smashing-down of the defective lamb, which seems to me present now. Well, to preview the Parousia is to experience the Parousia is to live through the Parousia, is to experience Christ as returned now. Thus my confusion between the idios and the koinos. The idios now, the koinos later (for everyone). This is the first time I've considered my experience from the standpoint of Heraclitus' distinction. His distinction makes it possible to suppose that I did indeed have the experience, even if no one else did. -2- More important, Heraclitus' distinction makes it evident where the Kingdom of God is (among you, within you); evidently it is currently limited to the idios kosmos. (Koinos later?) (As in "Thy Kingdom come," etc.). In fact without the distinction of Heraclitus it is impossible to comprehend or explain how I could have the experience, and it be real, and others could not. Aha. In his discussions of the Kingdom of God, Jesus clearly indicated a finding of it by individuals, as distinguished from its general arrival. So certain persons could individually enter it, as I did, before His return and the Kingdom arrived in the koinos. It seems to me that what Jesus said about his first incarnation —its purpose— was that he came here and sowed a small seed (the mustard seed) and someday will return to harvest the crop produced from that tiny seed. As Judge, Christ is the Reaper Himself, of the final harvest which He originally planted. * * The phosphere activity, drop in GABA, signalled anamnesis: memory restored of who I was (secondarily, why I was here). Thus I could not, would not, do what the Xerox letter et al. demanded. My true self & destiny were recalled (to me). Purpose, mission, identity. Reason for being here — where I had been and was, where I would go L see (the Parousia). Even the verdict upon z me. And: I was restored to what I had once been (powers & faculties), and restored to my fellows (who instructed me, the plasmatic atmos¬y pheric entities. The curtain for a time, long enough, was lifted. I saw the landscape as it truly was, and the powers behind it, good & antagonistic. The grand design (secrets of the cosmos), origin (the stars), agency (logos), and outcome (restitution), and the historic events I was part of (overthrow of the tyranny). visinhibition took place, firing began; the missing circuits came on at last; their time had come. And mine. Today I dreamed that on March 21st (siclI I) I was released from prison, to write my 300,000 word theological exegesis. I gather (1) throwing off the Xerox letter et al. was means, writing is the end; (2) it is the U.S. who have a vested interest in my not writing, not Soviet (obviously). (I was singing Joe Hill's final statement.) The 21st! They would have nabbed me the next day! Had they nabbed me, I would have broken fast, being a weak & frightened person. My defiance was always out of weakness, not strength. As to the Marxists, they always intended to subject my work to the "structured critics"; this is stated by Lem in his article accompanying UBIK and by Jack Vann; Vann names the desired critics: Lem & Rottensteiner. Lem says, "There is no telling what his work might have become had he come under the scrutiny of good critics" or some such statement; their plans & intentions are conspicuous here. Falling into the clutches of either would have doomed me, and in 3-74 I was about to fall one way or the other — it scarcely matters which. I would never have been my own man again..,and I was so close to this. Strong, vigorous actions were required by the spring of 74 to evade falling into one of their hands — actions I couldn't foresee needing to do. Responding the way I did to the Xerox letter was only the start; look what more I had to do vis-a-vis Lem et al.
